findings.excerpt: **Proof technique:** repeat the integral argument in $\mathbb F_2$ coefficients, where every bundle is canonically oriented and every manifold has a mod 2 fundamental class, and identify the mod 2 Euler class with the top Stiefel-Whitney class.
findings.symptom: The actual ItemBody HTML leaves the inline-math delimiters and TeX command in a text node in the technique banner; the standalone original screenshot visibly shows raw, CSS-uppercased ` $\MATHBB F_2$ ` in the banner. Ordinary body math on this item is KaTeX-rendered, so the leak is confined to technique-banner math.
findings.suggested_repair: Keep mathematical notation out of the plain-text proof-technique banner, or render the technique value through MathMarkdown before applying the expected uppercase banner styling. Preserve the explanatory prose in the proof body.

diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The item contrasts a unit algebraic intersection number with three actual intersections, then constructs the extra opposite-sign pair by a finger move. This is a concrete geometric configuration whose central distinction is hard to see from the count alone.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Show N as a schematic local 3D picture or clearly labelled projection of A0 and B={p}×S1 with one + intersection; show the disk finger crossing B and resulting three points labelled +,+,−. Indicate the original point remains + and the two new points have opposite signs. Mark as schematic and do not imply the diagram proves existence or the inverse-isotopy claim.
diagram_candidates.confidence: likely useful, not a rendering defect

diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The example is explicitly organized around the band turning a disk into an annulus, the belt S^0 meeting its two boundary circles, and a 2-handle attached to one circle to create exactly one intersection. The source cites handle figures for this setup.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Draw D^2 with the two attaching intervals, the oriented band and resulting annulus, mark the two belt points (one on each boundary circle), then highlight the chosen attaching circle and its unique belt intersection. Use arrows or orientation marks only if the induced disk orientation is unambiguous; label the mod-2 count 1 and the endpoint case n=2,k=1.
diagram_candidates.confidence: likely useful, not a rendering defect

diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The definition carefully distinguishes the unordered branch-pair set D(f) from its collision image Σ(f), specifically warning that a triple image produces three branch-pair elements but only one image point. This distinction is the main subtlety of the definition.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Use three local source sheets x1,x2,x3 mapping to a common r; show the three vertices {x1,x2},{x1,x3},{x2,x3} in D(f) each mapping to the single r in Σ(f). A second two-sheet example can indicate the bijective case. Label this a set-level schematic, not a transversality proof; avoid assigning a single sign to the triple image.
diagram_candidates.confidence: likely useful, not a rendering defect

diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The source gives the linear flow equations and identifies the forward-stable disk {u=0} and backward-unstable disk {v=0}; a phase portrait directly depicts those invariant axes and flow direction.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: In the two-dimensional case r=s=1, draw the saddle at the origin, arrows expanding along u and contracting along v, mark {u=0} as forward-stable and {v=0} as backward-unstable. State it is the r=s=1 slice of the general product flow.
